propositions: Proposed experiment: route unchanged macOS pytest default and integration tiers to an ephemeral APFS RAM disk mounted at /Volumes/RebarTests instead of runner.temp to reduce filesystem I/O overhead on the critical path.

Retention criterion: macOS default-suite and job wall times must improve by at least the larger of 5% or the observed recent-green variation versus the no-RAM control (predeclared floor: ≤16m33.7s default, ≤19m34.2s job) while Ubuntu remains within its observed range.

Experiment result: four independent RAM-disk treatment runs (31869753711, 31869919362, 31870391571, 31873067707) all ran slower than the matched no-RAM control 31868300174 (17m26s default / 20m36s job), ranging 18m26s–20m54.61s, failing to meet the retention threshold.

Secondary defects discovered and fixed: (1) intentionally owner-nonwritable workflow snapshot fixtures caused recursive basetemp cleanup to fail with PermissionError; (2) nested pytest subprocess inherited cacheprovider config causing test pollution; both repaired in scope.

Resolution: rejected the RAM-disk hypothesis; reverted the experimental lifecycle and restored both pytest tiers to runner.temp; no test selectors, markers, assertions, workers, timeouts, platforms, or coverage behavior changed.
